title: Model Discrimination & Calibration Atlas — What Would Make One Explanation Better Than Another?
purpose: Move project testing beyond 'can mathematics be attached?' toward discriminating predictions, calibration, uncertainty, negative controls, competing models and explicit failure conditions.

claim_ladder.question: Is the object/relationship described clearly and reproducibly?
Is there a measured pattern beyond anecdotal selection?
Is there a formal mechanism producing observables?
Can parameters be estimated from declared data without arbitrary tuning?
Does the model predict something meaningfully different from plausible alternatives?
Does performance survive new samples, contexts or independent reproduction?
Do interventions, natural experiments or mechanism-specific evidence support the proposed causal story?

required: prediction made before evaluation where possible
negative control or placebo where meaningful
out-of-sample or holdout strategy where meaningful

model_comparison.rule: Always ask what a simple null/baseline explains before invoking a richer project model.
Compare against at least one plausible non-project explanation, not only random noise.
A more flexible model must earn its extra parameters through predictive or explanatory gain.
Inspect where the model fails, not only fit summary.
Vary reasonable preprocessing, thresholds and priors to see whether conclusions are fragile.
State the population/domain to which the test applies before generalizing elsewhere.

uncertainty_types.meaning: Uncertainty because available cases are a subset of a larger population.
Range of model parameter values compatible with data.
Uncertainty about the model form itself.
Multiple meanings can fit the same factual pattern.

negative_controls: Randomize or permute labels/links when appropriate to test whether a pattern survives arbitrary structure.
Use non-matching time windows or comparison groups where domain logic permits.
Fit alternative geometries to a claimed spiral/shape rather than judging visual resemblance.
Compare derivative versus independent sources when measuring corroboration.
Test whether a symbolic mapping still seems unique after generating plausible alternative mappings.
promotion_rules: A formal equation without measurable variables remains conceptual/formal, not empirically validated.
A good in-sample fit without comparison or holdout is insufficient for strong promotion.
A single successful prediction does not validate unrelated metaphysical claims attached to the same symbol.
Failure should downgrade or narrow the claim rather than being reinterpreted automatically as confirmation.
Replicable null results belong in the archive because they constrain future theory.

worked_test_cards.claim: An observed trajectory is better described as a spiral than as a closed circular/ring recurrence.
observables: position or phase coordinate over repeated cycles
baseline_models: closed circle/ring with recurrence and approximately zero net change in the chosen state coordinate
worked_test_cards.project_model: recurrence plus systematic change in at least one declared coordinate
worked_test_cards.discriminating_observation: After one or more nominal cycles, the system returns near the prior angular/phase position while a pre-declared state coordinate changes beyond uncertainty in a consistent direction or structured sequence.
worked_test_cards.failure_condition: If the alleged non-returning coordinate shows no reproducible change beyond noise, or arbitrary coordinate choice is required after seeing the data, the spiral claim is not supported over the simpler recurrence model.
worked_test_cards.negative_control: Fit the same analysis to a known periodic/closed process and verify that the method does not manufacture directional change.
worked_test_cards.lesson: Visual resemblance to a spiral is insufficient; the extra coordinate must be measured and pre-specified.

worked_test_cards.claim: A support system behaves more like the project Garden model when it increases durable distributed capability rather than preserving dependence on the central supporter.
baseline_models: resource transfer with no durable capability gain
centralized service model where outcomes collapse when support is removed
worked_test_cards.project_model: support that increases local competence, options, resilience and continued function after central support declines
worked_test_cards.discriminating_observation: Participants retain or improve function, choice and resilience after support is reduced, with lower dependence on the central node than before intervention.
worked_test_cards.failure_condition: Outputs improve only while the center remains indispensable, or capability/exit options do not improve despite resource transfer.
worked_test_cards.negative_control: Compare with a matched intervention that delivers similar short-term resources but no capacity-building component.
worked_test_cards.lesson: Good intentions and short-term outputs do not establish Garden-like generativity; downstream autonomous capacity is the test.

worked_test_cards.claim: Multiple visible references constitute independent corroboration only when their evidence roots are materially independent.
baseline_models: single-origin story copied through many outlets
worked_test_cards.project_model: corroboration strength follows independent evidence roots rather than visible repetition count
worked_test_cards.discriminating_observation: When references are collapsed by shared upstream source, effective independent-source count falls; claims with genuinely independent roots should retain support after deduplication.
worked_test_cards.failure_condition: If deduplication does not improve error detection or prediction of later corrections, the proposed independence model adds little value.
worked_test_cards.negative_control: Use a deliberately syndicated/press-release-derived story where many outlets are known to share one origin.
worked_test_cards.lesson: A large archive can still contain only one witness.

worked_test_cards.claim: A symbolic mapping is structurally informative only if it fits declared constraints better than plausible alternative mappings generated without hindsight.
baseline_models: random or permutation mappings preserving simple frequencies
worked_test_cards.project_model: pre-declared relation set that predicts additional mappings or exclusions with fewer arbitrary choices
worked_test_cards.discriminating_observation: The chosen mapping outperforms permutation/alternative mappings on pre-declared criteria and predicts new cases that were not used to construct it.
worked_test_cards.failure_condition: Many alternative mappings score similarly, or the fit depends on changing rules after inspecting each case.
worked_test_cards.negative_control: Generate shuffled label assignments and quantify how often comparably persuasive correspondences appear.
worked_test_cards.lesson: Meaningful symbolism can remain philosophically valuable even when uniqueness testing fails; failure only limits empirical/formal claims.
